Area.evidence_source: Of those in our sample who had attempted suicide, there appeared to be a clear difference between the one-offs, nearly all of whom portrayed themselves as having significant control of their lives at the time of interview, and those who had made repeated attempts on their own lives. The latter's low level of perceived control can also be seen as restricted agency, which we can speculate may have been related to past traumas, negative identities and constraining social structures.
